title: US Parents Say Having a Baby Is Too Expensive
paragraphs: A new baby is a cause for happiness and celebration. But a baby also comes with large costs, from diapers and formula to car seats and childcare.

A survey by the University of Michigan found that four out of five American parents think the cost of having a baby is now just too high. The survey included around 2,000 US adults who are parents of at least one child aged zero to 18.

Nearly all parents included in the survey agreed that early development is important to a child's long-term health. However, giving a child what they need at a young age has often meant parents need to cut their spending, work extra hours or use secondhand items.

The survey found that parents of younger children are especially affected by the cost of having kids, with two in five describing their family's financial situation as either "struggling" or "just getting by." And 37% of parents in these two groups said they worry about money all the time.

A lot of parents of older children haven't forgotten how difficult the first few years can be though, with 38% saying they have donated to organizations to help families with young children in the past two years.

Many parents would also support government programs to make things easier for new parents. Three in four support the idea of a state program to give paid leave during pregnancy and during the first few weeks or months of a baby's life.

Six in 10 also said they would support programs to give families in need baby formula or healthy food, while more than half support the idea of free or lower-cost childcare, as well as free car seats and diapers.
